title: 82.9% voted no.
description:
82.9% voted no. A national referendum on switching from left-hand to right-hand traffic failed by a landslide; only 15.5% voted in favour.

Twelve years later, they switched. The Riksdag approved the change in 1963 under pressure from the Council of Europe and the Nordic Council; overriding the 1955 vote.

3 September, 5:00 a.m. A loudspeaker announcement; 'Nu är det dags att byta!' ('Now is the time to change!'); and the whole country moved to the right side of the road at once.

Around 350,000 road signs changed overnight. Most were swapped in the 24 hours before the switch. The whole operation cost 628 million kronor.

The crash rate didn't spike. It fell.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dagen_H - established the exact switch time and date (3 September 1967, 05:00, with a 01:00-06:00 non-essential traffic ban), the sign count (around 350,000, including 20,000 in Stockholm), the Högertrafikkommissionen (HTK), the song contest detail, and border/vehicle statistics.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1955_Swedish_driving_side_referendum - established the exact 1955 referendum date (16 October 1955) and vote breakdown: 15.50% in favour, 82.89% against, 53.18% turnout; and that the Riksdag approved the switch anyway in 1963.
- https://www.amusingplanet.com/2019/04/dagen-h-day-sweden-switched-traffic.html - established the changeover cost (628 million kronor), the sign count (~360,000), and the 4:50 a.m. loudspeaker announcement detail.
- https://historyfacts.com/world-history/fact/sweden-switched-driving-left-to-right/ - independently corroborated the 5:00 a.m. switch time, the sign count, and that accident and injury numbers on the day and the following Monday were flat-to-down versus the national average, not spiked.
